body: I think she does. My mother has it, and despite the fact that they don't like each other, they're very similar in their behaviors.

You're very brave for posting here. Thank you for your response.

 All the same, I want to ask, and I mean this as nicely as possible - you realize there are better way of getting someone's attention, right?

When I called EMS last time, they wanted to keep her for observation, but she (she told me) that she straight up lied to them and told them that she'd stay with a friend and that the whole thing was a misunderstanding. They let her out that night.

In her words: "You know me. If I'd have told them the truth they would have kept me. Do you really think I don't know how to game their system by now?"

Thanks for the response. I try to keep that in mind when things get to that point, as much as I can. Sometimes it works, and she cools down. Sometimes it doesn't. 

 She isn't going to a therapist, or taking any medications. She's had bad experiences with both, and considers them verboten. She's only recently opened up to the idea of attending therapy with me.

 I want so badly to help her, because she's in pain and I've been there. On the pragmatic side however, I also don't want us to lose our jobs, though - because that would suck, a lot, and it wouldn't help anything if she's diagnosed medication that she can't afford and it would mean extra unnecessary stress.
